name: Ninety-Nine
about: The New Intern, NINETY-NINE: a static-web narrative game, one continuous first-person walk down through a real (photoreal) building that houses a fake (low-poly PS1) company. Eight scenes, two choices each, walked rather than clicked; the score picks each room's compliant or hostile render and one of four endings.

docs.role: Doc 1, the master source of truth: premise, spine and render, state model, canon C1 to C8, scene breakdowns, text library, combinatorics, open questions
Doc 2, the generation pipeline (Higgsfield stills, Kling motion and audio); its stills and clips were removed when the game became 3D-only
Doc 3, the mini-game UX spec: retired 2026-10-03, kept as the record of what was built and replaced
Doc 4, the technical build: stack, state module, manifest, renderer, audio, preloading, bail-out, tests, budgets

stages.title: Overview and the argument
prompts: In one sentence, what should the player feel at the final card, when the word "you" appears for the only time?
Doc 1 §9.1 argues that the absence of a good ending is the argument. Do you still stand by it?
Who is it for first: you, a few friends, or strangers who find it on GitHub Pages?
What should this teardown help you decide next?

stages.title: The interface that is not there
prompts: Doc 4 §14 bans non-diegetic buttons: EXIT and the sound toggle are all that is left. Is even EXIT one too many?
Threshold labels stand over the place to walk to. Should they ever lie, or stay strictly truthful?
Phone or desktop first: which one do you play it on yourself?

stages.title: Sets, scenes and endings as data
prompts: rooms.json is built by build_rooms.py and scenes.json is hand-edited. Is that split the right one, or should scenes be built too?
Who should author a new scene later: only you, or someone else working from the data alone?
The beat vocabulary keeps growing. Where would you stop it?

stages.title: Spine, render and the walked choice
prompts: Retiring the mini-games for walked thresholds was the largest change. What made you decide it?
Friction now comes from hesitation and doubling back. Should the player ever be told that it counts?
Which scene do you consider finished, and which still feels like a placeholder?
How long should one run take, and should a second run feel different?

stages.title: Engine, audio and tests
prompts: The test suite runs in a browser by hand, with an optional headless runner. Should it become CI?
The 48 Hz drone (C7) is one oscillator that never restarts. Is it the game's most important system, or one among several?
What is the slowest device it must run on?

stages.title: The building and the canon
prompts: The building's mood in three words?
Which canon rule (C1 to C8) would you defend if you had to break all the others?
Doc 1 §9.3 asks whether Harlowe deserves more. What is your answer now?

stages.title: Art, audio and the asset pipelines
prompts: Hand-built Blender sets, Higgsfield scene-builder projects, or the live three.js rooms: which is the game's real face now?
The generated stills and clips were removed. Is there anything from that era you miss?
What should the building sound like when nothing is happening?

stages.title: How it was made: history and reversals
prompts: The game went from generated video to a continuous 3D walk. Was the video era a detour, or a necessary sketch?
Which decision would you make differently with what you know now?
Was building it in AI sessions faster, or did the reviews cost more than they saved?

stages.title: Future: what is stale and what is next
prompts: The Blender and Higgsfield sets are stale since the continuous building. Rebuild them, or let them go?
What is the one thing that would make it finished?
What would make you stop working on it?
